I am 78 years old, and I have farmed these same 5 mu in Quzhou County for 55 years. I only finished primary school, but the land has been my real teacher. My household has six mouths, and my son and grandson work off-farm in Handan, though they always come back for wheat harvest and maize planting. With only my daughter-in-law and me for daily labor, I cannot manage too much land intensively, so I keep 4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 1 mu in cotton.

For the winter wheat on the 4 mu, I will rotary till the soil in early October and sow the improved *shimai* variety — about 30 jin of seed per mu, the same as my neighbors. I will spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then topdress with urea when the wheat turns green and again at jointing. That is about 30 jin of nitrogen per mu in total. I will irrigate three times: once before the freeze to protect the roots, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I also spray three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice for the aphids that always come. I expect around 950 jin per mu if spring does not dry out.

For the summer maize, there is no time to waste after wheat harvest in early June. I will plant hybrid *nongda372* directly into the stubble without tilling — just open the rows and drop the seed. One package per mu is enough. I will put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, and if the leaves look pale at the big-flare stage, I will add a little urea. About 22 jin of nitrogen per mu in total. I will irrigate twice: right after sowing if the soil is dry, and again when the tassels appear. Three sprays — herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borers. With decent weather, I should get about 1,050 jin per mu.

For the cotton on the remaining 1 mu, I will rotary till in mid-April and sow improved *guoxinmian* — about 2 jin per mu. Cotton brings good cash, but it is heavy work. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress twice more during flowering and boll-setting. About 18 jin of nitrogen per mu. I will irrigate three times through the hot summer. The bollworms never rest, so I will walk the sprayer across that mu about 13 times from June to September. It is tiring, but for 1 mu I can still manage. I hope for 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I do not experiment much anymore. At my age, stability matters more than chasing higher yields. I watch what the successful farmers in my village do, and I do roughly the same. Last year was acceptable, so this year I will follow the same path.
